subject: Galvanize: on-prem cluster topology and storage alignment
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@galvanizehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:18:00Z
Subject: Galvanize: on-prem cluster topology and storage alignment

Hi Lucas —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to capture the high-level constraints and a proposed set of decisions so we can lock the architecture before the onsite workshop. Please review and flag anything we missed.

Summary of what we heard from your side:
- Single customer rack at their primary site with 3x compute racks planned over two adjacent rooms
- Want a dedicated private cluster (no shared tenants) behind your corporate firewall; traffic to Redwood control plane will be egress-restricted
- Prefer block storage for model artifacts and stateful shards; logs/metrics can be on a shared NFS
- HSM/KMS mandatory for envelope key wrapping; SOC/compliance team will audit encryption integration

Proposed architecture decisions (draft):
1) Cluster topology:
   - 3 control-plane VMs (HA), colocated across two fault domains (room A/B) with anti-affinity
   - Node pools: 
     * inference-gpu: 8x GPU nodes (A100 40GB or equivalent) for live inference with taints/tolerations
     * batch-cpu: 6x CPU-only worker nodes for background jobs and quantization pipelines
     * infra: 2x smaller nodes for monitoring/CI/CD runners, logging collectors
2) Storage:
   - Primary block store: Rook/Ceph with CSI for provisioned RWO/RWX block PVs (encrypted at rest)
   - Fast-ssd storage-class for model volumes (io-heavy) with replication factor 2 across racks
   - NFS/samba export for long-retention logs and shared artifacts (ReadWriteMany)
   - PV reclaim policy: Retain for model volumes; snapshot backup daily to object gateway (on-prem S3)
3) Encryption & keys:
   - Integrate cluster CSI with your KMS/HSM via KMIP/KMS plugin; we'll validate flow in workshop
4) Networking:
   - Calico for CNI + network policy; service mesh optional (defer to phase 2)
   - MetalLB in BGP mode with your top-of-rack switches for stable external IPs
   - Egress via NAT gateway; we'll define egress IP allowlist for Redwood control plane endpoints

Open questions for Galvanize action before workshop:
- Confirm HSM vendor and whether KMIP endpoints are reachable from control plane subnets
- Preferred Rook/Ceph replication factor and preferred failure domain (rack vs room)
- Any prohibition on MetalLB (some sites prefer cloud LB appliances)

Attachments: galvanize-site-network-diagram.pdf (please attach your latest site diagram)

If that looks OK I’ll schedule a 2hr technical workshop (on-site) and bring a runbook draft + node sizing spreadsheet. Proposed times: Nov 30–Dec 2; I pasted a calendly link below for slot selection.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0126

Neha —

This summary looks great and aligned with what our infra team expects. A few clarifications from our side:
- HSM vendor: Thales Luna (we have a cluster reachable over our management VLAN)
- Storage preference: we want block-level volume for model shards; Ceph is acceptable if the team can provide operational runbook (our ops likes Rook but will accept vendor-managed Ceph)
- Replication: prefer rack-level replication (RF=2) given space constraints
- MetalLB: acceptable if we run BGP with our leaf switches; we will need configuration snippets for our network team

Questions: 
1) Do you recommend using Retain for PVs for model volumes? We plan to do offline artifact cleanup but want to avoid accidental data loss.
2) For snapshots, can your tooling push snapshots to our on-prem object gateway (minio)?

I'll attach our current site diagram and the brief from our SOC team for the KMS piece.

Thanks —
Lucas
Ops Lead, Galvanize Health

Thanks — quick technical notes from infra perspective. I captured a few concrete recommendations we should validate during the workshop:

Control plane & etcd:
- 3x control-plane VMs (2vCPU/8GB minimal each) is the minimum; given ETCD write load from model state, recommend 4vCPU/16GB per control-plane for headroom
- Pin etcd to dedicated disks (nvme) with proper IOPS guarantees

Node pools sizing:
- inference-gpu pool: target node spec = dual-socket 2U with A100 40GB (or L40s) + 512GB RAM; set qos to Guaranteed for model processes; use local nvme for ephemeral cache (lifetime = pod lifecycle)
- batch-cpu: c6i-equivalent 32vCPU / 256GB RAM; use cheaper SATA-backed volumes for model staging

Storage decisions:
- Rook/Ceph is our recommendation given on-prem; choose Cephfs for RWX where needed and RBD for block/RWO volumes for low-latency model mounts
- encryption: use Ceph's dm-crypt integration or LUKS on each OSD + KMS for key wrapping to meet your SOC needs
- snapshots: we can export scheduled snapshots via radosgw to your MinIO S3 endpoint — requires network path and creds from your side
- reclaim policy: Retain for model volumes (to avoid accidental deletion during pod churn). We'll include a cleanup playbook for owners to delete obsolete PVs

Networking & LB:
- MetalLB BGP is stable; we'll provide sample BGP config for your leaf switches. If your team prefers, we can instead hand traffic to an existing F5 using an internal VIP gateway
- Calico eBPF mode recommended for performance (unless constrained by kernel/operator constraints)

Operational runbooks & telemetry:
- We'll draft an ops playbook covering node replacement, OSD OOM/eviction behaviour, and PV restore runbooks
- Monitoring: Prometheus + node-exporter + MGR Ceph metrics; propose alert thresholds for OSD utilization and journal latency

Attachments I added for the workshop prep: galvanize-node-sizing.xlsx, kms-integration-checklist.pdf

Action items (owner in parens):
- Share Thales Luna KMIP endpoint details and test credentials (Galvanize)
- Confirm replication domain (rack vs room) — Lucas to confirm (Galvanize)
- Redwood to draft workshop agenda and node/service runbook (Neha/Karthik)

-Karthik
Principal Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.ai]
